chapters.title: Report Builder formulas
chapters.subtitle: Calculated fields that work like a spreadsheet

steps.text: The data of a report rarely has the number you need: minutes instead of seconds, a Long or Short label, an answer rate. A calculated field works it out with a formula, like a spreadsheet. This video builds five of them, in the Report Builder.

chapters.title: Why formulas
chapters.subtitle: The value the data does not have

steps.text: A report shows what is stored: seconds of waiting, dates, names. People ask for minutes, labels, ages in days, and rates.
A calculated field is a formula with a name. Once it exists, you drag it onto columns, filters and visuals like any other field.
A formula never stops the report: dividing by zero or a missing value gives an empty result.

chapters.title: Add a calculated field
chapters.subtitle: Label, name, formula, check and apply

steps.text: This report lists calls. In the Data pane, under Calculated fields, click New.
Enter a Label, such as Wait in minutes, and a Name that formulas will use: a letter first, then letters, digits and underscores. The name cannot be changed later.
Write the Formula. Click a field in the Fields list, and it is written for you, in square brackets. Then divide it by sixty.
Click Check. The builder shows the type of the result, or what is wrong. Click Apply.
The new field is listed under Calculated fields. Drag it onto Columns, and the preview shows it for every call.
A formula can give a label. This one answers Long when the talk time is ten minutes or more, and Short otherwise. Text goes in quotes.
A formula can fill a gap. COALESCE gives the queue name, or Outbound campaigns when a call has no queue.
And a formula can work with dates. DATEDIFF counts the days from the call to today. The Functions list explains every function, and a click writes it into the formula.
A formula that uses an aggregate function, such as SUM or COUNT, is worked out once for each group. This report counts calls for each queue.

The answer rate adds one for each call that has an answer time, and divides by the number of calls. Inside such a formula, every field must be inside an aggregate function, and Check tells you when one is not.
Apply it, drag it onto Columns, and give it the format P zero, so it shows as a percentage. Each queue now has its rate.
Minutes, not seconds: divide the seconds, and give the column a format with one decimal.
A label to group by: Large and Small orders, Long and Short calls, or Business and Personal email addresses.
A rate once per group: answered over offered, converted over created, refunded over sold.
A calculated field is a formula with a name. Check it, apply it, and drag it wherever a field goes. Other features of the site can add functions of their own. Thanks for watching.
